- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–4 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); cap forecast at 10–15% below true if sentiment is neutral or negative.
